title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: In how many ways can \(345\) be written as the sum of an increasing sequence of two or more consecutive positive integers?

solutions.text:
A sum of consecutive integers equals the count times the median. For an odd number of terms, the median is an integer divisor of \(345,\) giving runs of \(3\) (median \(115\)), \(5\) (median \(69\)), \(15\) (median \(23\)), and \(23\) (median \(15\)) terms. For an even number of terms the median is a half-integer. The positive possibilities have lengths \(2,6,10,\) with respective medians \(172.5,57.5,34.5.\) Longer divisor-based runs would force a nonpositive first term. This gives \(4+3=7\) ways.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: A run of \(k\) consecutive integers equals \(k\) times its median, and \(345=3\cdot5\cdot23\)
For odd \(k,\) the median is an integer factor; for even \(k,\) the median is a half-integer. Count both while keeping all terms positive
